name: Ernst Vierkötter
highlight: A Cologne swimmer who broke the Channel record in 1926 and won Toronto’s inaugural 21-mile marathon swim in 1927.
biography: Ernst Vierkötter of Cologne took up the family bakery after his father died. On 30 August 1926 he became the fastest swimmer to cross the English Channel. His registered time of 12 hours 38 minutes lowered Gertrude Ederle’s mark by 2 hours 1 minute. Georges Michel swam faster the following month.

The Channel registers list a solo crossing from France to England. Captain Salmon piloted the escort vessel Europe. The historical register gives clocks of 13:32 and 02:10, while contemporary German reporting describes an early-morning departure and an afternoon finish. Exact local clock times remain unresolved.

The following summer Vierkötter won the Canadian National Exhibition’s 21-mile Lake Ontario swim. The organiser’s historical table gives 11 hours 45 minutes. A race-day report says the announced time was corrected to 11 hours 42 minutes 12 seconds. He settled in Toronto and later taught swimming and officiated at the exhibition.

Cold water stopped every starter in the 1928 men’s race. Vierkötter covered 12 of the 15 miles in 7:39:37 and shared in the prize money. He completed the 15 miles the next year, finishing second in 8:31:39.3. In 1930 he placed fifth in 8:30:10.4.

lines.label: Route
lines.text: Contemporary reports identify Cap Gris-Nez and the Dover coast. The individual registers give country-level endpoints.

lines.label: Pilot and vessel
lines.text: Captain Salmon aboard Europe. The German newspaper spells the vessel Europa.

lines.label: Recorded clocks
lines.text: 13:32 departure and 02:10 arrival in the historical register. The time standard is unspecified.

lines.label: Alternative account
lines.text: A contemporary report describes departure around 01:35 and an afternoon finish near Dover. The exact local clocks remain unresolved.

lines.label: Timing discrepancy
lines.text: The detailed registers agree on 12h38. The Dover biography gives 12h40 and the German report gives 12h42.

lines.label: Record
lines.text: Fastest France-to-England crossing at the time. Georges Michel lowered the mark to 11h05 that September.

lines.label: Recognition
lines.text: Listed by the Channel Swimming Association. The historical database identifies the CSA as ratifier.
The register spellings differ, but the year, German sporting nationality, one-way direction and duration identify the same crossing.

lines.label: Event
lines.text: 21-mile open race on Lake Ontario, Toronto

lines.label: Time
lines.text: 11 hours 45 minutes in the organiser’s programme. The contemporary race report gives a corrected time of 11:42:12. The exact finish time remains disputed.

lines.label: Status
lines.text: Did not finish. None of the 199 starters completed the 15-mile course.

lines.label: Prize
lines.text: One of fourteen swimmers who received an equal share of the purse.

lines.label: Date evidence
lines.text: The 31 August race report places the race on the previous day. A later directory lists 28 August.

questions.label: How fast did Ernst Vierkötter swim the English Channel?
questions.value: His registered time on 30 August 1926 was 12 hours 38 minutes, from France to England.

questions.label: Who piloted Ernst Vierkötter’s Channel swim?
questions.value: The historical register identifies Captain Salmon and the vessel Europe.

questions.label: Did Ernst Vierkötter finish the 1928 Toronto marathon swim?
questions.value: He covered 12 of the 15 miles. None of the 199 starters finished. His second-place finish was in 1929.
